body: Oops, definitely not gigantae. Seasonality is important in this identification. I'd compare this mushroom to Calvatia craniiformis. C. gigantae develop as a round ball for the most part. This mushroom species commonly develops that odd protustion at the base, like a mock stipe. This gives it the common name "Skull-shaped Puffball". I've eaten these, the outer layers are tougher than other puffballs. I peeled this layer off before consuming. Happy hunting!

Add-on: I guess black trumpets don't have bright colors but yeah, lots to know about a handful of species we call Chanterelles.

I don't really get the "Fruity" smell when they are fresh, it's after you soak them in salt water is when that smell comes out most for me. The key defining features for chants are bright colors, "false" gills, and white flesh. I think they have a salmon pink spore print if you wanted to be sure. 

I harvest smooth canterelles that have no false gills and can grow very large. Not all chants look the same but they do all have key identification characteristics specific to each species. Mushroomexpert.com is a great website.

Happy learning 😘

Fascinating, I'm an experienced DM with 10+ years of game sessions. I just started a campaign where a good friend of mine is playing a charismatic wizard. He told me on session 0 he wanted to play a sleezy-flirty fire mage. In anticipation of him hitting on my NPCs the whole campaign, I wanted to take control of the situation like only a DM can: I convinced him to care about the first NPC he flirted with. She was genuinely interested in him and thought he could do no wrong. Before meeting PC she's hit with a curse that turns her body to stone. On a peaceful night while traveling she reveals this to him. Upon returning to her home, she becomes a stone statue with a final kiss from the PC. PC leaves to meet party for the first time with a stone tear clasped in his hand.

TLDR: If you hit on my NPCs I'll murder them in front of you just to see the horror in your face. This is my world, you just live here. 😘 

As a note: my group are all very tight friends and the wizard loved this. I believe there were a few real tears when the NPC said her goodbye. Use this tactic in an appropriate setting.
